transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-04-08 11:30 PT | Duration 42m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Ellen Park (Redwood CSM); Marcus Lee (Cedar ML Eng), Sofia Gomez (Cedar PM), Tom Nguyen (Cedar Data Eng), Leah Ortiz (Cedar Security)

Summary (auto): Weekly POC sync to review KV/prefix cache hit-rate improvements from last week, discuss prompt reuse strategy, surface regressions in hallucination for cached completions, and agree on next steps for benchmark and config rollouts.

00:00 Jared: cool uh thanks everyone for joining, we'll keep to 45. quick round-robin for updates, priya you want to start?
00:18 Priya: yeah sure, um so quick summary of what we ran since last sync, we pushed the prompt-canonicalization layer and toggled prefix trimming for the 3 high-volume routes, also increased kv cache size for those pools, and we collected hit-rate snapshots over 72 hours.
00:35 Marcus: yep saw that, thanks. preliminary numbers look promising but we have some weird variability at 2am jobs.
00:46 Priya: right so headline: aggregate KV hit-rate jumped from ~18% baseline to 42% average across the three routes; prefix-level caching (the early tokens) improved token reuse by about 1.6x. those are rolling means, std dev is... uh higher than we'd like.
01:05 Tom: are those client-side normalizations included? we did some pre-processing on our side too.
01:12 Priya: good call, Tom — the reported numbers are server-side observed keys. we asked you to stop client-side canonicalization last Thursday to isolate effects, were those changes turned off?
01:23 Marcus: i thought they were off, but i did a quick check and there are still a few lambda jobs that append session ids to the prompt. my bad.
01:28 Jared: okay that's probably contributing to the 2am variance then. suggestion: we can add a server-side "strip-session-ish" rule in the prefix layer to canonicalize those ephemeral tokens, we have a sample script. i'll send it.
01:40 Sofia: can you explain what you mean by prefix trimming vs canonicalization? we heard both terms in last call and want to be sure we don't break product logic.
01:50 Priya: yeah so prefix trimming is a short heuristic: drop very long system preambles beyond N tokens for cache key calculation only; canonicalization is mapping multiple semantically-equivalent prompt variants to the same key — like normalizing timestamps, anonymizing user names, removing UUIDs. trimming is cheaper but less powerful. canonicalization is more work but gives higher hit rates.
02:12 Leah: from security perspective we don't want server-side modifications that could leak PII. how does Redwood handle anonymization?
02:20 Priya: great question, Leah. our script runs deterministic regex replacements and never sends the original removed segments to storage; keys are hashed locally with customer-controlled salt in Private deployments, and in hosted mode we use tenant-scoped keyed hashing. we will also provide a config to run canonicalization only on metadata-copy for cache key generation, not the user-visible request body.
02:40 Leah: ok will need a short write-up for compliance review.
02:45 Jared: we'll attach that in the security bundle.
02:48 03:00 Priya: digging into anomalies: the 2am jobs show drop in hit-rate from 52% down to 18% for one route; we traced that to an ETL job that injects environment debug lines ("--debug-run id=...") into the prompt mid-stream, which changed the key for every call. once we excluded that job, hit-rate returned to steady state.
03:25 Marcus: right, that's our nightly enrichment pipeline, missed that one. will patch.
03:30 Priya: another observation: for route B we saw higher cache hits but occasional quality regressions — i.e., cached completions were slightly stale when prompts included recent context variables (order numbers). on a cold miss the model returned fresh text, but the cached response was older and occasionally mentioned the wrong order number.
03:53 Tom: that sounds bad — is there TTL on cached completions?
03:55 Priya: yes, default TTL is 6 hours for the POC config, but we allowed some responses to be cached with TTLs up to 24h by mistake when we flipped the batch config. we flagged that and set route-level overrides so you can specify a per-template TTL.
04:15 Marcus: okay let's keep TTL shorter for anything with mutable fields.
04:20 Sofia: can we detect mutation-prone templates automatically? perhaps using a simple heuristic that looks for tokens like order_id, invoice, date, etc.
04:28 Priya: we have an experimental heuristic in the optimizer that tags keys as "volatile" if they contain placeholders like <ORDER_ID>. we can run it in audit mode first and show false positives.
04:40 Jared: question for Redwood SEs — what kind of ops overhead are we expecting if we turn on full canonicalization on all routes?
04:49 Priya: CPU-wise it's minimal; most of the canonicalization is regex and small token transforms. however, it does add a tiny bit of latency (~6-12ms p50) at the pre-cache compute path. the tradeoff is substantially fewer model calls and lower per-token cost overall. in our test, the net p99 latency for end-to-end fell by 10% when hit rates improved because fewer cold misses went to the model.
05:12 Marcus: can you share that benchmark? we need to show ops that net savings justify the complexity.
05:18 Priya: yes i'll attach the loadbench CSV and traces. (note: attach links) -> https://redwood.example/sigs/cedar/poc/loadbench-0408.csv and https://redwood.example/sigs/cedar/poc/traces/flame-0408.zip
05:30 Tom: about the hashing — we saw collisions? some distinct prompts mapped to the same key once we enabled a custom salt.
05:36 Priya: collisions were very rare; what looked like collisions were mostly canonicalization overreach where two prompts were normalized to the same canonical form. we can toggle canonicalization strictness.
05:48 Jared: recommended path: 1) run canonicalization in audit-only for 48-72h; 2) produce top-50 candidate merges for your team to sign off; 3) flip to enforced mode for the low-risk templates; 4) keep TTL conservative for templates with dynamic tokens.
06:10 Marcus: that seems fine. timeline: we can do audit this week.
06:14 Priya: on instrumentation — we added new tags to the per-token trace: key_generation_time, canonicalization_variant, and cache_lookup_ms so you can slice by variant and time-of-day. we've also surfaced a small dashboard widget showing raw/normalized key ratios.
06:30 Sofia: i saw the dashboard but it's confusing which column is normalized. any chance you can highlight normalized ratio per route?
06:36 Priya: yes, we'll update the widget to show: raw_requests / normalized_keys / hit_rate. i'll push that change.
06:44 07:00 Leah: on compliance please confirm that normalized snippets are not stored in plain text in our logs.
07:07 Priya: confirmed — normalized snippets used for key generation are hashed before persistent storage, and ephemeral copies are garbage collected within 10 minutes in hosted mode; in Private we can provide private-only logs. we'll add a small note in the security PDF.
07:23 Marcus: ok good.
07:28 Jared: quick dashboard numbers we saw: after the fixes you pushed the rolling 24h hit-rate for route A is 46% (up from 18%), route B 39% (up from 21%), route C 41% (up from 17%). overall token-level savings ~27% which maps to projected cost reduction of ~19% given your token mix.
07:57 Tom: where did the 27% come from? is that accounting for bigger completions due to cached outputs being longer?
08:04 Priya: yes it's token-level: we multiply average tokens avoided per hit * hit-rate. we also subtract small added cost from canonicalization compute. linked formula is in the doc we shared.
08:18 Marcus: noticed one more thing: sometimes the prefix cache returns an older templated paragraph that refers to product names we have renamed. that causes user-facing errors. is there a way to invalidate keys based on a content flag?
08:32 Priya: yes we support metadata-driven eviction. you can attach a tag to a model version like "product_v2" and as soon as a new deployment goes live you can trigger a namespace purge or selective evict by tag. we can demo that.
08:49 Jared: next up: we'll propose concrete config changes. i'll run through our recommendation now.
08:56 Jared: recommendation snapshot: enable canonicalization audit across all routes for 72h, run explicit mapping review for top-50 normalized merges, set TTL default to 1h for templates with placeholders, add 48-hour golden-directory for product name renames to auto-evict, and run nightly loadbench with the canonicalization in audit mode.
09:20 Marcus: ok good, i like the 1h TTL default.
09:25 Sofia: on the pilot scope — once audit looks good can we rollout in a canary to 10% traffic?
09:30 Priya: yes Redwood supports percent-based routing at the model-route level; we can do 10% canary, monitor hit-rate, latency, and quality signals for 48h, then expand.
09:40 Tom: what quality signals do you recommend? we saw a small but measurable regression score on the rouge-like metric for a handful of templates.
09:48 Priya: recommended signals: (1) prompt->completion semantic drift via embedding similarity vs baseline, (2) token-level mismatch for placeholders via regex checks, (3) customer QA thumb-rate if you have manual labels. we can pump all three to the same alert rule.
10:10 Marcus: about alerts — can we get an alert when cache-hit drops >10% vs baseline or when normalized keys change by >15% in an hour?
10:18 Priya: yes both doable, we'll create a rule and give you an incident channel hook (PagerDuty/Slack).
10:24 Jared: okay to recap next steps: Jared will send the canonicalization script and sample dashboard, Priya will run the 8k token loadbench and share traces, Marcus will audit client jobs and remove ephemeral tokens, Leah will review the security blurb. we'll also schedule canary after audit.
10:45 Marcus: yep
10:47 Leah: noted
10:48 Sofia: thanks all
10:50 Jared: cool will follow up in email with attachments. thanks everyone.
